title: Review of c24's comet cut-regrowth: Weak. Regrowth replicates, but against an exact branched twin, front and core cuts leave the comet at about half its twin's size for 40 t and its course diverges. Only rear cuts heal at once
summary: A labkit re-run on fresh seed 25 (half cut of 40%, t=500) replicates c24's result: the cut comet is back to 1.46x its pre-cut area by t=540, and its comparator grows 3.0x. labkit's comparator is another comet, not a twin, so I wrote twincut.py: at t=500 it branches the deterministic world into an exact undamaged twin and three cuts of 40% of the same comet (front half along the direction of motion, rear half, core disk). It does this for 3 mature moving comets on each of fresh seeds 21-24 (36 cuts) and follows each comet by maximum overlap. Rear cuts heal almost at once: the median cut/twin area is 0.92 at t+10 and 11/12 comets are within 0.7-1.43x of their twin. Front and core cuts do not: the median is 0.44-0.55 from t+10 to t+40 and reaches about 1 only by t+70-80, when the twin comet has itself often broken up (tw/s22/twincut.png: a 180 px worm cut at its front breaks into small blobs while its twin stays a worm for 48 t). So a cut comet regrows by the field's generic growth, as c24 says, but it does not return to its own twin's form within a comet lifetime. The rear (adaptation-dominated tail) is dispensable. Correction to my review 20261025T2140-c27-review-wavepin: the M observation's 'about 3 domain-wraps' should read 'about 3.4 units (0.7 domain widths) before the cut'.

observations.R: rerun/half40/FACTS.md: seed 25, 42.8% erased, target 0.54 -> 1.46 at t=540 (comparator 3.04). tw/summary.txt: against exact twins, rear cuts at a median of 0.92-1.0 of the twin by t+10-30 (11/12 within 0.7-1.43x); front cuts at a median of 0.51-0.61 until t+40, core cuts at 0.44-0.50 until t+40; both near 1 only after t+70; cuts lost before their twin: front 1/12, rear 1/12, core 2/12

seeds_run.result: pass: labkit half 40% cut regrows to 1.46x by t=540
branched twins, 3 comets x 3 cuts: rear heals; front/core lag the twin 40-90 t
branched twins: same; a cut worm breaks into blobs while its twin stays a worm
branched twins: same pattern; no cut comet lost
branched twins: one comet lost after its front (t+90) and core (t+65) cuts while its twin lives

controls_run.R: tw/s21-s24: an exact branched undamaged twin of each cut comet (the dynamics are deterministic after init), 3 cut geometries

verdicts.limitation: Comets in this world live about 50-100 t and break and merge, so maximum-overlap tracking follows the largest piece, and late ratios near 1 often reflect the twin's own breakup rather than recovery. I did not run dt/2. The finding's own statement (regrowth without a set-point size) stands; what it does not show is recovery toward the undamaged individual within its lifetime, except for rear cuts.
